back: Remove or change exactly one component of a system, holding everything else (data, budget, tuning effort) fixed, to measure that component's contribution.
Pass 1 (5-10 min): title, abstract, headings, figures, conclusion. Pass 2: text, figures and setup, list claims and evidence. Pass 3: re-derive/re-implement, find assumptions and failure cases.
Claim, evidence (which table/figure), baseline, what is missing.
If you cannot recover the published baseline number, a comparison with it is meaningless.
Quantities that must hold by construction (initial loss near ln K, zero-mean advantages, gradient check). A violation signals a bug before you interpret results.
A single run is one random draw (init, batch order); seed-to-seed spread can be larger than the effect you are measuring.
Report mean and sample standard deviation (ddof=1) over n seeds, and state n and what the seed controls.
Use the same seeds (same init and batch order) for both arms so that noise cancels in the per-seed difference.
$d_i=a_i-b_i$; $t=\bar d/(s_d/\sqrt n)$ with $n-1$ degrees of freedom (critical value 2.776 for 4 d.o.f., 5% two-sided).
$t=(\bar a-\bar b)/\sqrt{s_a^2/n+s_b^2/n}$; ignores pairing, so with large seed noise it has much less power.
A tiny effect can be significant with enough pairing/data; always report the effect size in the metric's own units.

front: Absence of significance is not equality
back: With few seeds you may lack power. Report an interval and the effect sizes you could have detected.
Tune the baseline as carefully as the new method and give it the same budget (steps, parameters, compute); otherwise the gain is an artefact.
Observation: accuracy rose 4.4 points. Interpretation: because of saturation. Mark untested interpretations as hypotheses.
Shadow: run the new model in parallel without serving it. A/B: randomly split live traffic and test significance. Canary: gradually roll out and abort if metrics degrade.
Gain below seed noise, single run, weak/untuned baseline, tuning on test data, unequal budgets, no ablations, claims beyond tested settings.
